presentation.label: Euclidean SEQ
presentation.summary: A track window that writes Euclidean rhythms, parameter lock rhythms and in-scale melodies into the pattern, for audio and MIDI tracks.
presentation.overview: Hold [TRACK] and press [PAGE] to open SEQ on that track. The rhythm page spreads PULS hits over the track length and turns them with ROT. LANE chooses whether A, B and the step grid edit the TRIG rhythm (sample trigs or note trigs) or the PLCK rhythm (parameter locks on their own steps). D picks the page and parameter to lock, E (DPTH) how far the locks move around the Part's value. [RIGHT] opens Harmony for PTCH or NOTE: a scale, a root, a phrase shape and a jump size, plus voices and chords on MIDI tracks. [YES] writes the result into the pattern as ordinary trigs and locks, so it plays, saves and copies like anything you program by hand.
highlights: Euclidean TRIG and PLCK rhythms up to 64 steps, drawn as a 4 x 16 step grid.
Parameter lock rhythms for any page-1 parameter the LFO can reach on audio tracks, and every page-1 parameter on MIDI tracks.
Harmony page for PTCH and NOTE: scale, root, phrase (RAND, UP, DOWN, ALT, TRI) and jump size; voices and chords on MIDI tracks.
[CUE] released alone places random hits on the focused lane; [FUNC] + [BANK] clears SEQ's locks or trigs on the track.
usage: Hold [TRACK] and press [PAGE]: SEQ opens on that track. Press another [TRACK] to switch, [MIDI] to move between the audio and MIDI track.
Turn A (PULS) and B (ROT) to shape the rhythm in the step grid, then press [YES] to write it into the pattern.
Turn C to PLCK, pick a parameter with D and a depth with E, then [YES]: that parameter gets locks on its own rhythm. [NO] closes SEQ.

limitations: OS 1.40C on the Modwerk base, over USB. Tested on the author's MKII with RAM-booted development twin 4c7eb79b; emulator rollback cases are recorded in TESTING.md.
The octabam module's FX page-2 destinations and CX OSC SETUP destinations are left out: D offers page-1 parameters only. A seq.work from octabam keeps them and loads here unchanged.
Keep SEQ installed while you save, reload or copy a project that uses it: without it, seq.work is not saved or reloaded with the project.
A seq.work SEQ cannot read is left as it is and SEQ starts from its defaults; the next save copies it to seq.bak before writing a new one.

storage.label: Storage
storage.conditions: The package is 36,760 bytes of code and data (module:dev --build-only); seq.work is about 9 KB per project. Not yet measured on a unit.

processing.label: CPU / DSP load
processing.conditions: SEQ runs only in the UI task while its window is open and in the project-file task; it adds nothing to the frame interrupt. Not yet measured on a unit.

tests.summary: Partial MKII and emulator results are recorded in TESTING.md; full publication qualification remains incomplete.
gates: Unit trial over USB: open, write, clear and close on audio and MIDI tracks; seq.work saved and reloaded

license.declaration: SEQ is ilia-murzinov's original work, ported from his octabam module (MIT). No Elektron firmware, extracted routines or tables: stock sites are named by address, length and SHA-256.

access.location: Any track page: hold [TRACK] and press [PAGE]
steps: Hold a [TRACK] key and press [PAGE]: the SEQ window opens on that track.
Turn A to D to set the rhythm, the lane and the parameter; [LEFT] and [RIGHT] switch between the rhythm and Harmony pages.
Press [YES] to write the rhythm and locks into the pattern, or [NO] to close SEQ.
